content.text: No MFN language exists anywhere in the agreement, and the only related provision runs in our favour.

input.quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or price/terms-parity obligation in either direction. I read the entire document (single section, paragraphs p0000–p0074) and searched for "most favored nation", "no less favorable", "favourable", "third party terms" and "best" — no clause requires AP to extend to Kubient any pricing, revenue share or other terms it grants to third parties, and nothing requires AP to match third-party offers. Section 5 (p0023) leaves revenue sharing to individual Exhibits without any parity undertaking, and Section 1 (p0001) expressly confirms the arrangement is non-exclusive and does not restrict AP from offering Inventory through other agents or selling Inventory to third parties — language that benefits us and is the opposite of an MFN burden. This meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer), so no redline is warranted. Note for diligence only: the fee Exhibits are not part of this document, so if any Exhibit or order form later introduces a parity or rate-matching covenant running in Kubient's favour, it should be reviewed against this rule.
